solution.why_others_wrong: April 1988 is DFHI; November 1986 the 182-day T-bill; June 1997 the 14-day T-bill.

fact_checks.claim: Mar 1989: Certificates of Deposit (CDs) and Commercial Paper (CPs) introduced in India to widen the monetary instruments

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.subtopic: Instruments: T-bills, CP, CD, call money
questions.question_text: In RBI's Treasury Bill auction of 4 November 2026, notified at ₹8,000 crore each for 91-day and 182-day bills and ₹7,000 crore for 364-day bills, what happened in the 182-day auction?

options.text: The full ₹8,000 crore was accepted at a yield of 5.90%
It was oversubscribed and accepted at 6.65%
It was converted into a cash management bill

solution.explanation: RBI accepted the full amounts in the 91-day (cut-off yield about 5.90%) and 364-day (about 6.65%) auctions, but the face value accepted in the 182-day auction was nil.
solution.why_others_wrong: 5.90% and 6.65% were the 91-day and 364-day yields; no conversion took place.
solution.final_answer: Option B: No bids were accepted

fact_checks.claim: T-Bill auction result November 04, 2026: 91-day ₹8,000 crore accepted (YTM 5.8970%); 182-day total face value accepted NIL; 364-day ₹7,000 crore accepted (YTM 6.6485%)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.subtopic: Instruments: T-bills, CP, CD, call money
questions.question_text: During the 1973 oil shock, the call money rate rose to an all-time high. What was it, and what did the Indian Banks' Association do?

options.text: 30%; IBA intervened and fixed a ceiling of 15%

solution.explanation: RBI's chronology says the call money rate rose to an all-time high of 30% in 1973, prompting the IBA to intervene and fix a ceiling of 15%.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other figures and actions are not recorded.
solution.final_answer: Option D: 30%; IBA intervened and fixed a ceiling of 15%

fact_checks.claim: 1973: Call money rate rose to an all time high of 30% prompting the Indian Banks' Association to intervene and fix a ceiling of 15%

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.subtopic: Instruments: T-bills, CP, CD, call money
questions.question_text: Under RBI's non-competitive bidding facility for retail investors in G-sec and T-bill auctions, what share of the notified amount is set aside, and how do investors participate?

options.text: Up to 5% of the notified amount, through an aggregator such as a scheduled bank, primary dealer or specified stock exchange
Up to 2%, only through mutual funds

solution.explanation: Non-competitive bids up to 5% of the notified amount are allowed within it. Retail investors cannot bid directly; they come through an aggregator/facilitator, with a minimum bid of ₹10,000, and are allotted at the weighted average price of competitive bids.
solution.why_others_wrong: 25%, 10% (that is for SDLs) and 2% are not the facility for central auctions; the routes are wrong.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Up to 5% of the notified amount, through an aggregator such as a scheduled bank, primary dealer or specified stock exchange

fact_checks.claim: Non-competitive bids up to 5 per cent of the notified amount will be allowed; eligible investors have to come through an aggregator or facilitator (Scheduled Bank, Primary Dealer or Specified Stock Exchange); minimum amount Rs.10,000

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.subtopic: Instruments: T-bills, CP, CD, call money
questions.question_text: In a T-bill auction notified at ₹8,000 crore, the non-competitive segment (5% of the notified amount) receives bids of ₹500 crore. An investor bids ₹10 lakh through her bank, which charges the maximum permitted commission. What does she get, and what is the commission?

options.text: ₹8 lakh of T-bills; commission up to ₹480

solution.explanation: Reserved amount = 5% × 8,000 = ₹400 crore. Bids of ₹500 crore exceed it, so allotment is pro rata: 400/500 = 80%, giving ₹8 lakh. The aggregator may recover up to 6 paise per ₹100: 8,00,000 / 100 × 0.06 = ₹480.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹10 lakh ignores pro-rata allotment; ₹800 uses 10 paise; ₹4 lakh halves the ratio.
solution.final_answer: Option A: ₹8 lakh of T-bills; commission up to ₹480

fact_checks.claim: Non-competitive bids up to 5 per cent of the notified amount; if the aggregate amount bid is more than the reserved amount, allotment would be made on a pro rata basis; the aggregator can recover up to six paise per Rs.100 as commission

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to SEBI, what is 'dabba trading'?

options.text: Illegal trading in which deals are settled internally by an operator without being executed on a recognised stock exchange
Trading in small-cap shares on the SME platform
Trading in government securities on NDS-OM

solution.explanation: SEBI describes dabba trading as an illegal, unregulated form of trading where deals are not executed on any SEBI-recognised exchange but settled internally by the dabba operator, leaving investors without exchange grievance redress or guaranteed settlement.
solution.why_others_wrong: SME trading, algo trading and NDS-OM trades are legitimate regulated activities.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Illegal trading in which deals are settled internally by an operator without being executed on a recognised stock exchange

fact_checks.claim: Dabba trading is an illegal and unregulated form of trading in securities; traders place deals without the trades actually being executed on any official SEBI recognized stock exchange; settled internally by the dabba operator

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: When an investor applies in an IPO through ASBA (Application Supported by Blocked Amount), what happens to the application money?

options.text: It is transferred to the issuer at once and refunded if shares are not allotted
It is held by the stock exchange until listing
It stays in her account, blocked and earning interest, and is debited only on allotment
It is moved to an escrow account and earns no interest

solution.explanation: Under ASBA the amount is blocked but remains in the investor's account until allotment, continues to earn interest, and is debited only on allotment; no refund is needed if shares are not allotted. UPI can be used as the payment mechanism.
solution.why_others_wrong: ASBA avoids transfer-and-refund, escrow without interest and exchange custody of funds.
solution.final_answer: Option C: It stays in her account, blocked and earning interest, and is debited only on allotment

fact_checks.claim: In ASBA, money to the extent of price of the shares applied for is blocked, but it remains in their account till allotment; blocked amount continues to earn interest and there is no requirement of refund in case of non-allotment

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: World Investor Week 2026, celebrated in India from 5 to 11 October 2026, is a global investor-awareness initiative of:

solution.explanation: SEBI's investor site describes World Investor Week as an IOSCO initiative for global investor awareness, celebrated every year by securities regulators; in India in 2026 it ran from 5 to 11 October.
solution.why_others_wrong: The IMF, BIS and World Bank do not run World Investor Week.
solution.final_answer: Option A: IOSCO (International Organization of Securities Commissions)

fact_checks.claim: World Investor Week 2026 initiative by IOSCO for global investor awareness campaign; it is being celebrated in India from October 5 to 11, 2026

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's chronology, which depository institution commenced operations in August 1988?

options.text: Stock Holding Corporation of India Ltd (SHCIL)

solution.explanation: RBI's chronology records that SHCIL, a depository institution, commenced operations in August 1988. NSDL came in 1996, CDSL in 1999 and CCIL in 2001.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other institutions came later.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Stock Holding Corporation of India Ltd (SHCIL)

fact_checks.claim: Aug 1988: Stock Holding Corporation of India Ltd. (SHCIL) a depository institution commenced operations

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
At its 215th meeting on 24 September 2026, SEBI's Board approved new Portfolio Managers Regulations, 2026. Consider:
I. Discretionary PMS may invest up to 10% of client AUM in investment-grade, non-convertible, unlisted debt securities with client consent.
II. Investment in exchange-traded derivatives is permitted up to 1.25 times the client's AUM.
III. The new regulations retain the 2020 regulations alongside them.
Which is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The Board approved PMS Regulations, 2026 in supersession of (not alongside) the 2020 regulations (III wrong). Measures include up to 10% of AUM in investment-grade unlisted NCDs under discretionary PMS with consent (I) and derivatives up to 1.25 times AUM (II).
solution.why_others_wrong: III is wrong; 'I only' omits II.
solution.final_answer: Option B: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: The Board approved the proposal to introduce SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2026 in supersession of SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2020; enabling investment upto 10% of client AUM in investment-grade, non-convertible, unlisted debt securities under DPMS with client consent; investment in Exchange traded Derivatives up to 1.25 times of client's AUM

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which set of items was among the approvals of SEBI's Board on 24 September 2026?

options.text: A ban on all IPOs on the SME platform
Settlement Regulations, 2026 replacing the 2018 settlement regulations, a Common Advertisement Code for specified regulated entities, and FPI participation in exchange-traded commodity derivatives
Abolition of the T+1 settlement cycle and a return to T+2

solution.explanation: PR No. 59/2026 lists approvals including the SEBI Settlement Regulations, 2026 (replacing the 2018 regulations, in force from the day after the 30th day from notification), a Common Advertisement Code, FPI participation in ETCDs, Vault Manager amendments, DRs on REIT/InvIT units and a Settlement Scheme for illiquid stock options.
solution.why_others_wrong: None of the other measures was approved.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Settlement Regulations, 2026 replacing the 2018 settlement regulations, a Common Advertisement Code for specified regulated entities, and FPI participation in exchange-traded commodity derivatives

fact_checks.claim: 215th meeting of the SEBI Board: review of SEBI (Settlement Proceedings) Regulations, 2018; Common Advertisement Code for Specified SEBI Regulated Entities; FPI Participation in Exchange Traded Commodity Derivatives; Settlement Regulations, 2026 shall come into force the day succeeding the 30th day from the date of notification

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
At its meeting of 19 June 2026, the SEBI Board revisited share buybacks. Consider:
I. Open-market buybacks through stock exchanges were reinstated, with effect from 1 August 2026.
II. Promoters remain barred from participating in such buybacks.
III. All forms of buyback, including tender offers, were abolished.
Which is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The Board amended the Buy-back Regulations, 2018 to reinstate open-market buybacks via exchanges from 1 August 2026, with promoters still not allowed to participate. Buybacks were not abolished (III wrong).
solution.why_others_wrong: III is wrong; 'I only' omits II.
solution.final_answer: Option D: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: SEBI board reinstated open-market buybacks through stock exchanges, effective August 1, 2026, with promoters barred from participating

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: SEBI's investor advisory (August 2024) on companies listed on the SME segment described a pattern used by some promoters. Which sequence matches it?

options.text: Listing only through the book-building route on the main board
Issuing only debt instruments to retail investors
Delisting the company to avoid disclosures
Exaggerated public claims about operations, followed by bonus issues, stock splits or preferential allotments, while promoters offload shares at inflated prices

solution.explanation: SEBI observed that some SME companies and promoters make exaggerated claims, follow them with corporate actions like bonus issues, stock splits or preferential allotments that create optimism, and then offload holdings at inflated prices. It advised investors to verify information and avoid tips.
steps: Hype → corporate actions → promoter selling at high prices
solution.why_others_wrong: Delisting, main-board book building and debt issues are not the described modus operandi.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Exaggerated public claims about operations, followed by bonus issues, stock splits or preferential allotments, while promoters offload shares at inflated prices

fact_checks.claim: Some companies and their promoters make exaggerated claims about their operations, followed by corporate actions like bonus issues, stock splits, or preferential allotments; promoters may exploit this to offload their holdings at higher prices

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017, what is the maximum compensation (including expenses) for which an Insurance Ombudsman can entertain a complaint?

solution.explanation: The Council for Insurance Ombudsmen states that the Ombudsman can entertain complaints where the compensation does not exceed ₹50 lakh, including relevant expenses.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹30 lakh is the RBI Ombudsman's consequential-loss cap; ₹20 lakh and ₹1 crore are wrong.

fact_checks.claim: The Insurance Ombudsman can entertain complaints where the compensation awarded does not exceed rupees 50 Lakhs (including relevant expenses, if any)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The 'Committee on Reform of the Insurance Sector' constituted in 1994 was chaired by:

solution.explanation: RBI's chronology records the 1994 Committee on Reform of the Insurance Sector under R. N. Malhotra, whose recommendations led to opening of the sector and to IRDA.
solution.why_others_wrong: Narasimham chaired banking reform committees; Tarapore capital account convertibility; Rangarajan other panels.

fact_checks.claim: 1994: 'Committee on Reform of the Insurance Sector', RN Malhotra

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Within what time must a policyholder approach the Insurance Ombudsman under the 2017 Rules?

options.text: Within 30 days of the claim event
Within one year of the insurer's rejection or reply, or of the expiry of one month without a reply
Within three years of buying the policy
Within 90 days of the insurer's reply

solution.explanation: A complaint must first be made to the insurer. A representation can be made to the Ombudsman within one year from the insurer's rejection/reply, or after one month with no reply.
solution.why_others_wrong: 30 days, 90 days (RBI Ombudsman's window) and three years are not the rule.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Within one year of the insurer's rejection or reply, or of the expiry of one month without a reply

fact_checks.claim: A representation should stand made to the Insurance Ombudsman within one year from the date of the insurer's rejection/reply, or after the expiry of one month if no reply

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under IRDAI's master circular on health insurance (May 2024), within what time must insurers decide on a cashless authorisation request and on final authorisation after a discharge request?

options.text: Within one hour, and within three hours of the discharge request
Within 30 minutes, and within one hour
Within three hours, and within seven days

solution.explanation: The May 2024 master circular requires insurers to decide on cashless authorisation within one hour of request and to give final authorisation within three hours of the discharge request.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other timelines are not those prescribed.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Within one hour, and within three hours of the discharge request

fact_checks.claim: Insurers to decide on cashless authorisation within one hour of request and final authorisation within three hours of receipt of discharge request from the hospital (IRDAI master circular, May 29, 2024)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Besides personal lines and group policies, the Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 also cover policies issued to which kind of businesses?

solution.explanation: The Rules cover complaints on personal lines of insurance, group policies, and policies issued to sole proprietorships and micro enterprises.
steps: Coverage includes sole proprietorship and micro-enterprise policies
solution.why_others_wrong: Large companies, PSUs and reinsurers are outside this consumer forum.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Sole proprietorships and micro enterprises

fact_checks.claim: These Rules aim at resolving complaints relating to disputes with insurance companies on personal lines of insurance, group insurance policies, policies issued to sole proprietorship and micro enterprises

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the Insurance Ombudsman:
I. The institution of Insurance Ombudsman has been functioning since 1999.
II. Where a complaint is settled through mediation, the Ombudsman makes a recommendation within one month of receiving the parties' written consent.
III. A complainant may engage a lawyer to argue the case before the Ombudsman.
Which is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The Insurance Ombudsman has functioned since 1999 (I), and in mediation the Ombudsman makes a recommendation within one month of the written consent (II). The 2017 Rules have no provision for engaging a lawyer (III wrong).
solution.why_others_wrong: III is wrong; 'I only' omits II.
solution.final_answer: Option D: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: The Institution of Insurance Ombudsman has been established and is functioning since 1999; the Ombudsman shall make a recommendation within one month of the date of receipt of mutual written consent for mediation; as per the Insurance Ombudsman Rules 2017, there is no provision to engage a lawyer

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about IRDAI's master circular on health insurance of May 2024:
I. The moratorium period, after which a claim cannot be contested for non-disclosure, was cut from eight years to five years.
II. After the moratorium, a policy and claim can be contested only for established fraud.
III. Insurers may take up to 24 hours to decide a cashless authorisation request.
Which is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The moratorium was reduced from eight to five years (I), and afterwards claims are contestable only on established fraud (II). Cashless authorisation must be decided within one hour, not 24 hours (III wrong).
solution.why_others_wrong: III is wrong; 'I only' omits II.
solution.final_answer: Option C: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: The moratorium period is reduced from eight years to five; no policy and claim shall be contestable on grounds of non-disclosure except for established fraud after the moratorium; cashless authorisation within one hour

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

options.text: A tax statement issued by the Income Tax Department
A statement of a company's consolidated accounts
A single monthly statement of an investor's transactions across all mutual funds and holdings in demat accounts
A bank statement covering all savings accounts

steps: CAS = MF transactions + demat holdings in one statement
solution.why_others_wrong: It is not a bank, tax or company-accounts statement.
solution.final_answer: Option C: A single monthly statement of an investor's transactions across all mutual funds and holdings in demat accounts

fact_checks.claim: Consolidated Account Statement (CAS) is a single/combined account statement which shows the details of transactions made by an investor during a month across all Mutual Funds and also other securities held in their demat account(s)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In BE 2026-27, the Centre's tax revenue (net to Centre) is ₹28.67 lakh crore and non-tax revenue ₹6.66 lakh crore. What are revenue receipts, and roughly what share of them is non-tax revenue?

solution.explanation: Revenue receipts = net tax revenue + non-tax revenue = 28.67 + 6.66 = ₹35.33 lakh crore. NTR share = 6.66 ÷ 35.33 ≈ 18.9%. (6.66 ÷ 28.67 ≈ 23.2% is NTR relative to net tax, not to receipts.)
solution.why_others_wrong: 23.2% divides by net tax; ₹22.01 lakh crore subtracts; ₹44.04 lakh crore is gross tax revenue.

fact_checks.claim: The Tax Revenues (Net to Centre) are projected to be ₹28.67 lakh crore; NTR of the Central Government is projected at ₹6.66 lakh crore; Revenue Receipts estimated at ₹35.33 lakh crore

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In BE 2026-27, gross tax revenue (GTR) is ₹44.04 lakh crore, a growth of 8.0% over RE 2025-26, with direct taxes at ₹26.97 lakh crore and indirect taxes at ₹17.07 lakh crore. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Direct taxes are about 61.2% of GTR, and RE 2025-26 GTR was about ₹47.6 lakh crore
Direct taxes are about 38.8% of GTR, and RE 2025-26 GTR was about ₹40.8 lakh crore
Indirect taxes are about 61.2% of GTR, and RE 2025-26 GTR was about ₹47.6 lakh crore
Direct taxes are about 61.2% of GTR, and RE 2025-26 GTR works out to about ₹40.8 lakh crore

solution.explanation: 26.97 + 17.07 = 44.04; direct share = 26.97 ÷ 44.04 ≈ 61.2%. RE 2025-26 GTR = 44.04 ÷ 1.08 ≈ ₹40.8 lakh crore (₹47.6 lakh crore would wrongly add 8%).
solution.why_others_wrong: Indirect taxes are 38.8%; 47.6 multiplies instead of dividing by 1.08.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Direct taxes are about 61.2% of GTR, and RE 2025-26 GTR works out to about ₹40.8 lakh crore

fact_checks.claim: In BE 2026-27, Gross Tax Revenue (GTR) is estimated at ₹44.04 lakh crore. It represents a growth of 8.0 per cent over RE 2025-26. Direct Taxes at ₹26.97 lakh crore are the major contributor to GTR (61.2 per cent of the GTR). Indirect taxes are estimated at ₹17.07 lakh crore

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

options.text: A: ₹48 lakh (30% tax + 30% additional tax); B: a fee of ₹1 lakh

Category B (asset up to ₹5 crore, income already taxed) pays a fee of ₹1 lakh for immunity from penalty and prosecution.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹24 lakh omits the additional 30%; B does not pay a percentage of the asset; A is not the full FMV.
solution.final_answer: Option C: A: ₹48 lakh (30% tax + 30% additional tax); B: a fee of ₹1 lakh

fact_checks.claim: For category (A), the limit of undisclosed income/asset is up to 1 crore rupees; they need to pay 30 percent of Fair Market Value as tax and 30 percent as additional income tax in lieu of penalty; for category (B), asset value up to 5 crore rupees; immunity with payment of fee of 1 lakh rupees
